longForm.heroLead: Rotor-stator homogenization works on a different principle than ultrasonic probes entirely: material gets drawn directly into the generator probe and exposed to intense mechanical and hydraulic shear as it passes through, not broken apart by cavitation bubbles. A 144W high-torque motor drives speeds from 5,000 to 35,000 rpm, processing 0.03mL to 500mL samples (up to 1L depending on probe and viscosity) through the PRO Quick Connect stainless-steel probe system. New thumb-operated speed control and a redesigned ergonomic housing keep operation one-handed, while the quick-connect system delivers secure coupling, reduced vibration, and easy cleaning every time a probe swaps out. Existing PRO Quick Connect probes stay compatible with this redesigned motor unit, so current ProScientific users can upgrade without replacing probes or accessories already on hand.

paragraphs: Understanding how rotor-stator homogenization actually works explains why it handles certain samples differently than an ultrasonic probe would. The generator probe draws material directly into itself, where it passes through the narrow gap between a rotating rotor and a fixed stator, experiencing both mechanical shear from the blade action and hydraulic shear from the turbulent flow that gap creates.

The PRO Quick Connect probe system is what makes switching between applications practical rather than a maintenance chore. Coupling stays secure during operation, vibration drops compared to less precise connection systems, and cleaning between samples is straightforward since the stainless-steel probe disconnects cleanly.

Complete homogenizing packages bundle the motor unit, generator probe, stand assembly, and accessories together for labs starting from scratch.

Worth knowing if your lab already runs an earlier-generation Bio-Gen PRO200: factory technical assistance, repair services, replacement parts, compatibility guidance, and upgrade support continue for legacy units wherever possible, and because the redesigned motor stays compatible with existing Quick Connect probes, upgrading often doesn't mean replacing everything at once.

faqs.question: How is PRO250 different from PRO200?
faqs.answer: PRO250 delivers more power, 576W versus 144W, and handles larger volumes, up to 5L versus PRO200's 500mL-1L range, though PRO200's top speed reaches higher at 35,000 rpm versus PRO250's 30,000 rpm.

faqs.question: How does the separate ON/OFF switch improve repeatability?
faqs.answer: The speed dial stays at your chosen setting independent of the ON/OFF switch, so switching off between samples and back on returns you to the exact same speed without re-adjusting.

faqs.question: What sample volumes can PRO250 handle?
faqs.answer: 0.03mL to 5L, with higher volumes dependent on sample viscosity.

faqs.question: Can PRO250 be used post-mounted rather than hand-held?
faqs.answer: Yes, it works both hand-held and post-mounted; pair it with a PRO250 Stand Assembly for stable, hands-free operation.

faqs.question: What probe sizes are available?
faqs.answer: PRO Quick Connect stainless-steel probes ranging from 5×75mm to 30×200mm.

faqs.question: How fast does PRO250 run?
faqs.answer: Variable speed from 10,000 to 30,000 rpm.

paragraphs: More power on its own doesn't guarantee repeatable results, it just processes faster. The separate ON/OFF switch is what actually delivers repeatability here: dial in your speed once, and every subsequent run starts at exactly that same setting, since switching off between samples doesn't reset the dial.

That power translates directly into volume headroom. 0.03mL to 5L is a genuinely wide range for one hand-held unit, and the 5×75mm to 30×200mm probe range gives you the physical reach to match probe size to sample volume rather than forcing every job through one probe geometry.
